results.title: Over 68% SIR enumeration forms digitised: ECI - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: elections_process/national: ECI's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and electoral roll digitisation progress.

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: The Election Commission of India (ECI) reported that over 68% of enumeration forms for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls have been digitised across 12 States and UTs.
notes.fact_box: The SIR is being conducted in 12 States/UTs including Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Lakshadweep. The enumeration phase began on November 4 and is scheduled to end on December 4, with the draft list publication set for December 9.

prelims_pointers.text: 34,86,60,338 enumeration forms (over 68% of existing electors) have been digitised as of November 27, 2025.
Lakshadweep and Goa are among the leading states in digitisation with 99.9% and 89.77% respectively.
Uttar Pradesh and Kerala are the lagging states with 47.59% and 55% digitisation respectively.
Booth-level officers (BLOs) are responsible for collecting filled-in forms and uploading data to the ECI website via dedicated apps.

notes.mains_question: Discuss the significance of digitising electoral rolls in ensuring the integrity of the democratic process and the challenges faced in achieving universal coverage.
mains_dimensions: Data integrity: Reducing manual entry errors and preventing duplicate entries through real-time app-based uploads by BLOs
Logistical bottlenecks: Disparity in digitisation rates between states like Lakshadweep and Uttar Pradesh highlighting infrastructure gaps
Transparency: Publicly accessible draft lists and formal grievance redressal mechanisms for claims and objections
